name: Mercedes-Benz 190E EVOLUTION II
description:
The Mercedes-Benz 190E Evolution II represents the ultimate expression of Mercedes-Benz's commitment to DTM (Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters) racing in the early 1990s. While the 190E compact sedan, introduced in 1982, quickly earned the affectionate nickname 'Baby-Benz,' few could have predicted it would evolve into one of the most extreme homologation specials ever created by the Stuttgart manufacturer.

Unveiled at the Geneva Motor Show in March 1990, the 190E 2.5-16 Evolution II was the final and most radical iteration in the 190E's motorsport evolution. To meet DTM homologation requirements, Mercedes-Benz produced exactly 502 units within just three months—a limited run that made the Evo II instantly collectible and highly sought-after.

The Evo II's most striking features were impossible to miss: a massive adjustable rear wing that dominated the car's profile, dramatically flared wheel arches to accommodate wider track and tires, and aggressive aerodynamic bodywork designed to maximize downforce and minimize drag. Every visual modification served a functional purpose, developed through extensive wind tunnel testing and racing experience.

Under the hood sat a highly developed 2.5-liter inline-four engine producing 235 horsepower in street trim, though the racing versions unleashed significantly more. This sophisticated powerplant featured 16 valves with DOHC, advanced engine management, and race-bred internals. The suspension, brakes, and chassis were similarly enhanced to exploit the aerodynamic improvements and deliver handling worthy of the car's racing pedigree.

The Evolution II wasn't just a homologation special—it was a statement of Mercedes-Benz's motorsport ambitions and engineering prowess. Today, it stands as one of the most iconic German performance cars of the era, bridging the gap between road car and race car with uncompromising purpose.
author: S.Stirpe
